questions.prompt: Which phrase is explicitly listed as a focus point for “Understanding the Lua Stack” in the supplied curriculum?
options: A requirement that all Lua hosts expose the same APIs.
A guarantee that bytecode and native extensions work across every Lua version.
A rule that example code is automatically executed by CodeLeaf.
questions.explanation: The supplied PDF lists “Stack indices and stack discipline” under Understanding the Lua Stack. Host/API and runtime claims still need to be scoped to the relevant environment.

questions.prompt: What result is documented for the static reference example in “Understanding the Lua Stack”?
options: The Lua stack contains integer 42 before the state is closed.
No output is produced by any code block in this lesson.
Every supported Lua runtime must print exactly “Lua 5.5”.
The example always raises an error before producing a result.
questions.answer_key: The Lua stack contains integer 42 before the state is closed.
questions.explanation: The documented reference result for this sample is 'The Lua stack contains integer 42 before the state is closed.'. CodeLeaf does not execute this block; run it locally and confirm the actual runtime/host matches the assumption.

questions.prompt: Before using “Understanding the Lua Stack” in a real application, which practice is most reliable?
options: Check the target Lua version and host API, then test a normal input and an edge/failure case.
Assume a short example is production-safe because it looks simple.
Ignore errors if the expected output appears once.
Treat LuaJIT, Luau, and stock Lua 5.5 as the same runtime.
questions.answer_key: Check the target Lua version and host API, then test a normal input and an edge/failure case.
questions.explanation: Runtime versions, embedding hosts, native ABI, and failure conditions can differ; validate assumptions in the actual target environment.
